blurb:
This is your reliable neighborhood Chinese spot on Sandy Plains. Strip mall location, no frills, but the food is consistent and the prices are easy on the wallet. Good for a weeknight takeout run or a quick sit-down dinner when you don't want to think too hard about where to go. Over 230 reviews at 4.1 stars for a low-key local spot is a solid track record.

The menu covers the familiar Chinese-American standards you already know, so you're not going in blind. Nothing here is going to surprise you, and that's kind of the point. Sometimes you just want what you know, done well, at a fair price.

Just plan around their schedule. They're closed on Tuesdays, don't open until noon on Saturdays, and only run from 3pm to 9pm on Sundays. Worth a quick check before you head over.

blurb:
If you've got hungry kids or a group that wants to eat a lot without spending a lot, Pacific Buffet on Chastain Meadows Pkwy is worth knowing about. All-you-can-eat setup with sushi, tempura, and a spread of American options mixed in. It's not trying to be fancy and it doesn't need to be. It just delivers solid volume at a price that doesn't hurt.

The sushi is what pulls most people in, and for a buffet it holds up well. The tempura is also a consistent go-to. My wife and I have done it as a low-key weeknight dinner when nobody wants to cook and it works perfectly for that.

Ratings are strong for a buffet with over 4,000 reviews, which tells you the crowd keeps coming back.

blurb:
Good spot on Whitlock if you want a casual lunch or an easy Friday dinner without driving far. The service gets solid marks from pretty much everyone who goes, and it's the kind of place that works well for a family lunch or grabbing a bite with a few people who don't feel like overthinking it.

The food leans toward comfort fare, and a few reviewers have mentioned it can run on the greasier side depending on what you order. Worth keeping that in mind if you're going lighter. That said, people who've flagged it still say they'd go back, so take it for what it is.

They're open until 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays, which gives you a little more flexibility if you're not rushing.

blurb:
This is the place I send people when a group can't agree on where to eat. It's a food hall right off the Square with around twenty vendors under one roof, covering everything from tacos to sushi to dessert. If you've got kids who all want something different, this solves that problem fast. Good for lunch, good for a Friday night out, good for pretty much any situation where you need options.

Because there are so many vendors rotating through, I'd recommend just walking the whole hall first before you commit. Different stalls are the crowd favorites at different times, so go in with an open mind rather than a locked-in plan.

Friday and Saturday they stay open until 10pm, which makes it a solid spot if you're hitting the Square for an evening and want to eat without making a reservation somewhere.

blurb:
My wife and I have a soft spot for this place. It's all-you-can-eat Brazilian barbecue, which sounds like a lot, but the execution is legit. Good for a Saturday night out when you want something a little different from the usual burger or pizza run. The vibe is relaxed and the pace is unhurried, which I appreciate.

The cheese bread is the thing everyone talks about and they're right to talk about it. It comes out warm and you will eat more of it than you planned. The feijoada stew is also worth trying if you want to go full Brazilian and not just stick to the grilled meats.

They also do breakfast, which a lot of people don't know about. Opens at 10am every day, so it's a solid option if you want something more than a drive-through before noon.
